description: This is the list type to hold the checkpointing object
for the interfaces to the various supported checkpointing mechanisms.

attributes.name: name
description: @todo add description

attributes.name: interface
description: The type of checkpointing to be used, e.g.
-hibernator
-cpr @todo no longer supported SGI kernel level checkpointing, remove
-cray-ckpt @todo no longer supported Cray kernel level checkpointing, remove
-transparent, using a checkpointing library like Condor
-userdefined, some user defined method
-application-level, same as userdefined, all interface commands except restart are used, @todo verify

attributes.name: ckpt_command
description: Commandline to be executed to initiate a checkpoint.

attributes.name: migr_command
description: Commandline to be executed to initiate a migration of a job (from one host to another one).

attributes.name: rest_command
description: Commandline to be executed to restart a checkpointed application.

attributes.name: ckpt_dir
description: A directory to which checkpoints shall be written.

attributes.name: when
description: When a checkpoint shall be written, one or a combination of:
n: no checkpoint is performed
s: when the execution service is shutdown
m: checkpoint every minimum CPU interval (see queue configuration)
x: when the job gets suspended
an interval: in the specified interval

attributes.name: signal
description: A Unix signal to be sent to the jobs process(es) in order to initiate a checkpoint.

attributes.name: job_pid
description: @todo not used and can be removed?

attributes.name: clean_command
description: Commandline to be executed after checkpointing to clean up.

attributes.name: joker
description: Placeholder which can be used for arbitrary data.
Its purpose is to be able to add new attributes without changing the spooling format.
It is a list of arbitrary type and it is spooled.
